analysis:
The only changed content in docs/architecture/inference.md is a date bump (line 3) and a new documentation paragraph at head lines 1960-1973. That paragraph says a JSON response_format (json_object/json_schema) on the Qwen template family now defaults to a closed/disabled thinking block. A caller's explicit reasoning.enabled, enable_thinking, chat_template_kwargs, reasoning effort or positive reasoning.max_tokens keeps the caller's choice. The coordinator prompt sidecar is said to mirror the rule so cache planning renders the same prompt. The supplied units (head lines 417-1215) show only unchanged surrounding text. The new paragraph itself falls outside the supplied line windows, so I reviewed it from the patch excerpt rather than from numbered source lines.

Security relevance: this is a prompt-rendering change, not a change to a trust boundary, key handling or attestation. The affected threat is T-041, the prefix-cache and prompt-contract identity. If the provider renders the prompt differently from the sidecar, the effect is a cache miss or hit mismatch. Cache scope is derived by the coordinator from the authenticated account, model build and prompt-contract ID, and it is not caller-controlled. This does not widen the at-rest or cross-tenant exposure already accepted as SEC-035. The paragraph states that the sidecar mirrors the rule and that public prompt vectors pin it. I cannot verify that from the supplied evidence, because the code changes (Qwen35TemplateFix and the sidecar) are not in this batch. If the code change exists in other batches, integration should check that provider and sidecar renderings are identical. A divergence would only cause cache-correctness or availability problems, not a confidentiality break. Because the code is outside the supplied evidence, I report no finding. No new endpoints, secrets or data flows are introduced by the documentation text.
